sentence_stem: I have never flown on a plane, so
correct_completion: I asked the flight attendant many questions.
full_sentence: I have never flown on a plane, so I asked the flight attendant many questions.
acceptable_variants: I checked the airport signs very carefully.
I felt nervous at the check-in desk.

options.text: I got on the plane without any worries.
options.why_wrong: Calm confidence does not follow logically from having no flying experience, so this result does not fit the stem.

options.text: I know exactly how the security check works.
options.why_wrong: Having never flown, the speaker would not know this, so the completion contradicts the first clause.

options.text: I asked the flight attendant many questions.
I have flown many times before.
options.why_wrong: This contradicts the present perfect 'never' in the stem and does not give a result of it.

grammar_focus: Present perfect with 'never' followed by a result clause introduced by 'so'
explanation: 'So' introduces the result of the first clause. The present perfect 'never' describes lack of experience, so the correct completion must show a logical result of that lack, such as asking questions for help.
translation: Hiç uçakla uçmadım, bu yüzden uçuş görevlisine birçok soru sordum.
